title: Antarctic Ozone Hole Is the Seventh Largest in 48 Years
paragraphs: Every year, a large hole forms in the ozone layer over Antarctica. The ozone layer is a thin part of the sky that protects life from strong sunlight. In November 2026, American scientists shared the numbers for this year's hole.

The 2026 hole was the seventh largest in 48 years of records. On September 18, it reached its widest size, about 27 million square kilometers. That is nearly as big as the record from the year 2000. The lowest ozone level above the South Pole was 105 units on October 17.

Scientists say strong winds high above Antarctica made the hole larger this year. However, the hole could have been even bigger without the Montreal Protocol, a 1987 agreement that stopped many harmful chemicals. Experts expect the ozone layer to recover by the 2070s.
